ACCEPTANCE TEST: Create a custom record with nozzle temperatures (230-250 °C) and bed temperatures (80-90 °C). Kill the application process, reopen the app, and verify that the saved custom record retains all temperature values and provenance metadata.
CONSEQUENCE: User-edited catalog records and custom filaments lose nozzle and bed temperature ranges upon saving. Process death or application restart clears these values, producing incomplete OpenSpool write intents missing temperature constraints.
EVIDENCE: In app/src/main/kotlin/net/jamesjennison/spoolio/data/Databases.kt, the CustomRecord Room entity defines only id, brand, material, product, colorName, colorHex, diameterMm, massG, and updatedAt columns. In MainViewModel.kt, saveCustom() persists a CustomRecord and converts it back via asCatalogEntry(), which hardcodes all nozzle and bed temperature fields to null.
FINDING: Custom and edited catalog records discard nozzle/bed temperatures, source revision, and per-field provenance during local database persistence.
REQUIRED CORRECTION: Extend the CustomRecord database entity schema to store nozzleMinC, nozzleMaxC, bedMinC, bedMaxC, sourceRevision, and provenance metadata. Update CustomDialog and MainViewModel.saveCustom() to collect, validate, and persist temperature ranges and provenance.

ACCEPTANCE TEST: Scan an OpenSpool tag containing temperature ranges, select 'Edit as a local record', and save the record without manual intervention; confirm that the local record saves successfully and retains the decoded temperatures.
CONSEQUENCE: Tapping 'Edit as a local record' after reading a valid OpenSpool tag results in immediate validation failure upon saving, and any temperature parameters stored on the physical tag are silently lost.
EVIDENCE: In MainViewModel.kt, decodedSeed() maps the decoded tag values into CustomSeed with color set to "" and omits min_temp, max_temp, bed_min_temp, and bed_max_temp. When saveCustom() is invoked, validateRecord() throws a ValidationException("Brand, material, product, and color are required").
FINDING: Decoded OpenSpool tags fail validation when saved locally because OpenSpool NDEF payloads lack a color name field and decoded temperatures are ignored.
REQUIRED CORRECTION: Modify decodedSeed() to extract min_temp, max_temp, bed_min_temp, and bed_max_temp from the decoded JsonValue map, provide a sensible default or derived color name when converting NDEF payloads, and update CustomDialog to expose temperature editing.

ACCEPTANCE TEST: Select three distinct catalog and custom items, restart the app, and confirm that the main view renders the three recent items and allows selecting them for NFC write intent preparation.
CONSEQUENCE: The application fails the core requirement to make recent records accessible in the UI, forcing users to re-search the catalog repeatedly for recently handled spools.
EVIDENCE: In app/src/main/kotlin/net/jamesjennison/spoolio/data/Databases.kt, UserDao exposes recents(): Flow<List<Recent>>. MainViewModel.kt inserts records into recents in select(), but never queries or exposes store.user.user().recents() to MainActivity.kt.
FINDING: Recents history is persisted to Room storage but is never retrieved or presented in the application UI.
REQUIRED CORRECTION: Expose the recents Flow from MainViewModel and add a Recents list section to the UI in MainActivity.kt allowing immediate re-selection and editing of recently accessed items.

ACCEPTANCE TEST: Create a custom record with nozzle/bed temperatures, restart the app, verify temperatures and per-field provenance are retained. Edit a catalog entry, replace the catalog, verify edited metadata and original source per field remain intact.
CONSEQUENCE: Users cannot store or preserve temperature settings or original per-field provenance for custom or edited records; violates explicit requirement to preserve temperatures and provenance through process death and catalog replacement/removal.
EVIDENCE: CustomRecord entity in Databases.kt has columns only for id,brand,material,product,color_name,color_hex,diameter_mm,mass_g,updated_at; no nozzle_min_c, nozzle_max_c, bed_min_c, bed_max_c, and no per-field source/provenance. CustomRecord.asCatalogEntry() in MainViewModel.kt maps all temperatures to null and sets sourceRevision='user' for every field. CustomDialog in MainActivity.kt exposes only brand/material/product/color/hex/diameter/mass, no temperature inputs. MainViewModel.decodedSeed() drops min_temp, max_temp, bed_min_temp, bed_max_temp from decoded tag values.
FINDING: Custom records and edited-catalog records cannot preserve temperatures or per-field provenance.
REQUIRED CORRECTION: Add temperature columns and per-field provenance columns to CustomRecord (or a normalized editing table). Extend custom UI and decodedSeed() to include temperature fields. Store original source per field for edited catalog records and preserve it across catalog replacement.

ACCEPTANCE TEST: Select several items, navigate to a recents screen, verify they are listed. Delete the corresponding catalog entries, then confirm recents still show the original metadata from snapshot.
CONSEQUENCE: Requirement 'recents usable in UI' is unmet; if a catalog entry is removed, the recent cannot display its original metadata.
EVIDENCE: UserDao.recents() is defined in Databases.kt but never called by any ViewModel or Composable. MainViewModel has no recents state and the UI (SpoolioApp in MainActivity.kt) shows only search, results, and detail. Recent.snapshotJson in MainViewModel.select() stores only package_id and source_revision, not full record data.
FINDING: Recents are recorded but never exposed in UI, and the stored snapshot is insufficient for catalog removal.
REQUIRED CORRECTION: Expose recents in a dedicated UI section (e.g., list or menu). Store full record snapshot or join with current catalog/custom records while preserving provenance and temperatures.

ACCEPTANCE TEST: Select a catalog entry, modify a field, save. Verify the edited record appears, original source/provenance is retained per field, and data survives catalog replacement.
CONSEQUENCE: Requirement 'review/edit metadata' for the bundled OFD catalog is not implemented; users cannot correct or augment catalog data locally.
EVIDENCE: Detail composable in MainActivity.kt displays metadata and offers only 'Prepare verified NFC write'; no edit button. The only local record creation is the FAB 'Custom filament' or editing a decoded tag. No function in MainViewModel converts a CatalogEntry to a Provenance.CATALOG_EDITED record.
FINDING: No local edit capability for catalog entries.
REQUIRED CORRECTION: Add an 'Edit locally' action in Detail that opens a pre-populated form (including temperatures) and saves a CATALOG_EDITED record preserving original values and per-field provenance.

ACCEPTANCE TEST: Enter a known package ID in the search field and verify matching catalog entries are returned.
CONSEQUENCE: Requirement 'search exact brand/product/color/package' is not fully satisfied; users cannot search by package ID.
EVIDENCE: catalog_fts Fts4 table in Databases.kt has columns brand, material, product, color_name only; package_id is absent. MainViewModel.search() builds an FTS query only against those columns.
FINDING: Search does not support package identifier.
REQUIRED CORRECTION: Add package_id to the FTS index or implement a separate exact package lookup integrated with search.

ACCEPTANCE TEST: Present a tag containing two valid OpenSpool records while in AWAITING_TAG; expect a rejection with duplicate/multiple OpenSpool message and no write.
CONSEQUENCE: A tag containing multiple valid OpenSpool records can be overwritten, silently losing data; violates strict duplicate validation and no silent loss.
EVIDENCE: In NfcCoordinator.handle(), existingOpenSpool list is built but only checked for unsupported records (firstOrNull { it !is DecodeResult.Supported }). If all existing OpenSpool records are Supported, no rejection occurs. decodeSingleOpenSpool() does reject records.size != 1 on read, but the write path bypasses this check and after overwrite consent writes a single record, potentially discarding extra OpenSpool records.
FINDING: Duplicate OpenSpool records on a tag are not rejected before write.
REQUIRED CORRECTION: Before writing, reject if the number of existing OpenSpool NDEF records is not exactly one, regardless of whether each is Supported.

ACCEPTANCE TEST: Induce WRITE_OUTCOME_UNKNOWN, tap Cancel, verify state returns to CANCELLED/DRAFT, journal is cleared, and a new write can be armed.
CONSEQUENCE: If a write outcome is unknown and reconciliation fails (e.g., different tag or mismatch), the user is stuck in UNKNOWN state with a persistent journal and cannot cancel, clear, or arm a new write without clearing app data.
EVIDENCE: WriteStateMachine.cancel() has a no-op for phase WRITE_OUTCOME_UNKNOWN because the conditional branch does nothing and the else branch is not reached. NfcCoordinator.cancel() then calls persistOrClear(), which for UNKNOWN re-saves the journal instead of clearing. The UI NfcPanel always shows Cancel for non-VERIFIED states, but clicking it has no effect.
FINDING: Cannot cancel or recover from WRITE_OUTCOME_UNKNOWN state.
REQUIRED CORRECTION: In cancel() for WRITE_OUTCOME_UNKNOWN, clear the journal and set state to CANCELLED or DRAFT, allowing re-arm.

ACCEPTANCE TEST: Modify a row in the existing catalog DB while keeping the count identical; on next launch, ensureCatalog should detect the mismatch and reinstall the correct catalog.
CONSEQUENCE: A corrupted or stale catalog database with the same number of rows is accepted silently, leading to incorrect offline data.
EVIDENCE: DataStore.ensureCatalog() contains `if(catalog.catalog().count()==expectedCount)return` before any digest validation or parsing. It only validates the compressed asset digest before initial insert; there is no verification of the existing DB generation against the current manifest.
FINDING: ensureCatalog skips verification if row count matches, without digest/content check.
REQUIRED CORRECTION: Store a content hash or generation ID in the database and verify it against the manifest before trusting; if mismatch, reinstall the complete validated generation.

ACCEPTANCE TEST: Feed a modified catalog fixture containing an invalid hex color or negative mass; confirm import fails cleanly or rejects the invalid record.
CONSEQUENCE: Malformed bundled catalog data could cause runtime crashes or invalid records in UI and NFC encode paths.
EVIDENCE: In DataStore.ensureCatalog(), TSV parsing only checks `f.size==17` and later package ID uniqueness/count. No validation is performed on color_hex format, diameter_mm numeric/range, mass_g positivity, temperature ranges, or non-empty required fields. `f[9].toInt()` can throw on invalid mass.
FINDING: Bundled catalog rows lack strict field validation.
REQUIRED CORRECTION: Validate each field using core validators (normalizeHex, BigDecimal, range checks) during import; reject the batch or invalid rows with clear errors.

ACCEPTANCE TEST: Read a canonical tag, tap 'Edit as a local record', then save with only brand, type, color_hex, diameter, and weight populated. Verify the record saves and product/colorName are optionally blank or defaulted without validation error.
CONSEQUENCE: For a canonical OpenSpool tag that lacks subtype and color name fields, the user cannot save a local record without manually entering placeholder values, causing poor UX and potential data loss.
EVIDENCE: MainViewModel.decodedSeed() returns CustomSeed with product = text("subtype") (empty for canonical OpenSpool records) and color = "" always. Filament.kt validateRecord() requires brand, material, product, and colorName to be non-blank. CustomDialog pre-populates these blanks, and saveCustom will set an error, preventing save.
FINDING: Saving a decoded canonical tag as a local record fails because required product and color name are blank.
REQUIRED CORRECTION: Make color name and/or product optional for custom records or derive a safe default while preserving original tag fields; do not block save on missing label-only fields.

ACCEPTANCE TEST: Physical test passes all hardware acceptance criteria, including on-device p95.
CONSEQUENCE: Cannot conclude readiness; latent NFC stack, tag compatibility, or timing issues may exist despite source correctness.
EVIDENCE: Evidence states 'No physical tag test' and 'Physical NTAG215/PAXX/independent-reader and on-device p95 acceptance are not yet met.' Package contains only compile/lint/unit test output, no real NFC hardware logs.
FINDING: Physical NTAG215/PAXX/independent-reader and on-device p95 acceptance are not yet met; source-only/mocked success does not prove runtime.
REQUIRED CORRECTION: Execute the required physical human gate: test on the Android2023 Razr with actual NTAG215 and PAXX tags, verify with an independent reader, and collect p95 acceptance metrics.
